definition: Maximizing the share of AI requests that succeed with acceptable quality within cost, latency and compute budgets.
details: Like manufacturing yield, the goal is fewer defective or wasted runs. Teams tune prompts, routing, retries, model choice and inference settings so more requests meet quality thresholds without overspending.

explainer.lead: Yield optimization maximizes the share of AI requests that succeed at acceptable quality within cost, latency and compute budgets. It matters because wasted or failed runs consume spend without producing usable output.

tiers.eli5: Like a factory trying to ship as many good products as possible per hour, it cuts down on requests that come out broken or wasted.
tiers.practitioner: Teams tune prompts, routing, retries, model choice and inference settings so more requests clear quality thresholds without overspending. A common pitfall is chasing yield with retries that quietly blow the latency and cost budgets.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally, it maximizes the fraction of requests meeting a quality threshold subject to cost, latency and compute constraints; no single standard formulation is fixed, and trade-offs among constraints limit achievable yield.

explainer.example: A team routes easy queries to a small model and hard ones to a large model, raising the share of answers above the quality bar while staying under the monthly budget.
